newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress opposes any budget amendments.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress opposes any budget amendments.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Tuesday that it would not support any amendment to the 1997/98 (April-March) budget on the floor of parliament.

"We will not support any cut motion or amendment proposed by any party on the floor of the house," Congress leader Pranab Mukherjee told reporters after a meeting of the policy-making Congress Working Committee.
Mukherjee said Congress leaders planned to meet Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on May 5 to discuss the budget, due to be taken up in parliament during a session starting on Wednesday.
Sharad Pawar, Congress leader in the lower house, told reporters that the Finance Bill, which includes tax and tariff proposals, would come up for a vote on May 12.
Last week, Gujral's cabinet adopted the 1997/98 budget which former finance minister P. Chidambaram presented to parliament on February 28.
